sources.title: EP260321a/SN 2026gzf: The Faintest Shock Breakout Associated with a Broad-Lined Supernova
A Multi-Wavelength View of the First Type Ic-BL Supernova with an Einstein Probe X-ray Shock Breakout
Shock breakout from mildly relativistic ejecta in a dense wind: the case of EP260321a/SN 2026gzf
Dual evidence case: SN 2026gzf choked-jet inference and RBH-1 merger reconstruction

evidence.statement: Einstein Probe detected the fast X-ray transient EP260321a, later associated with SN 2026gzf.
Follow-up observations associate EP260321a with the broad-lined Type Ic supernova SN 2026gzf at redshift approximately 0.0344.
The reported X-ray emission is thermal with kT about 160 eV and peak luminosity about 2.2e44 erg/s.

measurement.quantity: thermal X-ray spectral temperature and peak luminosity

evidence.statement: Deep later Chandra X-ray observations did not detect an X-ray afterglow; the study reports that these limits exclude afterglows comparable to known gamma-ray bursts or fast X-ray transients.
evidence.confidence: high for non-detection; interpretation depends on comparison model

evidence.statement: Radio follow-up from 5.8 to 54.5 days after the fast X-ray transient rules out an on-axis jet counterpart with isotropic-equivalent kinetic energy above 1e49 erg for circumburst densities above 1e-2 cm^-3, under the study assumptions.

measurement.value: E_K,iso > 1e49 excluded for n > 1e-2 under model assumptions

evidence.statement: If a successful relativistic jet was launched, the O'Connor et al. modeling requires low initial Lorentz factor and low kinetic energy for the stated wind-density regime.
evidence.confidence: conditional on afterglow and environment assumptions

evidence.statement: An independent shock-breakout model reproduces the X-ray properties using mildly relativistic ejecta interacting with a dense wind-like circumstellar medium.

claims.text: EP260321a is associated with the broad-lined Type Ic supernova SN 2026gzf.
The soft thermal X-ray transient is consistent with a shock-breakout origin.
claims.confidence: strongly supported by current modeling, but still interpretive

claims.text: A standard powerful on-axis relativistic jet/afterglow is disfavored for EP260321a/SN 2026gzf.
claims.confidence: high within the tested parameter regimes

claims.text: A weak, mildly relativistic outflow choked by the progenitor star is a proposed explanation for the event.
claims.confidence: plausible proposed interpretation; mechanism not directly observed

assumptions.description: The thermal X-ray signal is interpreted through shock-breakout models whose inferred physical parameters depend on the ejecta/CSM model.
Jet constraints depend on the adopted synchrotron-afterglow model and microphysical parameters.
Jet and radio/X-ray constraints depend on the assumed circumburst density or wind-density profile.
The choked-outflow interpretation assumes that the stellar explosion launched an outflow/jet whose propagation can be constrained indirectly even though the jet itself was not directly observed.

hypotheses.description: A weak, mildly relativistic outflow was launched and choked by the progenitor star.
A successful jet existed but was off-axis, low-energy, low-Lorentz-factor, or otherwise below current detection limits.
No astrophysically important jet is required; shock breakout and circumstellar interaction dominate the observed high-energy signal.
The event launched a standard powerful on-axis relativistic jet comparable to classical GRB afterglows.

discriminating_observations.description: Obtain or compile deeper late-time radio and X-ray constraints to separate a weak/off-axis surviving jet from a no-jet or choked-outflow scenario.

expected_outcomes.late_non_detection: Further restricts surviving energetic-jet parameter space, conditional on environment and microphysics.
expected_outcomes.emerging_afterglow: Would strengthen a successful off-axis or weak-jet interpretation and permit tighter energy/geometry inference.

discriminating_observations.description: Improve constraints on circumstellar density structure and progenitor mass loss so that jet and shock-breakout inferences are less degenerate with environment assumptions.

readiness.rationale: The X-ray transient and SN association are strongly supported; a choked jet/outflow should be described as an inference or proposed scenario, not as a directly observed mechanism.
Existing non-detections identify useful late-time radio/X-ray parameter space, but interpretation remains coupled to environment and afterglow assumptions.
A label such as 'choked jet' should carry model-dependent provenance rather than being converted into a ground-truth observational class.
A single event and model-dependent jet interpretation are insufficient by themselves for a robust population-level label or rate claim.

notes: This pilot intentionally encodes the choked-outflow explanation as model-dependent rather than directly observed.
Null fields mean the value has not been encoded from a verified source in this record; they must not be silently guessed.
